paragraphs: Franklin Resources, Inc. ("Franklin") is a holding company with subsidiaries operating under our Franklin Templeton® and/or subsidiary brand names. Franklin's common stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE") under the ticker symbol "BEN" and is included in the Standard & Poor's 500 Index. In this Annual Report, Franklin and its subsidiaries are collectively referred to as the "Company," and words such as "we," "us," "our" and similar terms refer to the Company. We have one operating segment, investment management and related services.

We offer our services and products under our various distinct brand names, including, but not limited to, Alcentra®, Apera®, Benefit Street Partners®, Brandywine Global Investment Management®, Canvas®, Clarion Partners®, ClearBridge Investments®, Fiduciary Trust International™, Franklin®, Franklin Mutual Series®, K2®, Legg Mason®, Lexington Partners®, O'Shaughnessy®, Putnam®, Royce®, Templeton® and Western Asset Management Company®. Unless otherwise indicated, our "funds" means the funds offered under our various brand names, which may include co-branded funds.

We are a global investment management organization with over $1.6 trillion in assets under management ("AUM") as of September 30, 2025. Our mission is to help clients achieve better outcomes through investment management expertise, wealth management and technology solutions. Through our specialist investment managers, we offer specialization on a global scale, bringing extensive capabilities in equity, fixed income, alternatives and multi-asset solutions. For over 75 years, we have been committed to providing clients with exceptional investment management services and have developed a globally diversified business, including through strategic acquisitions.

We provide our investment management and related services to retail, institutional and high-net-worth investors in jurisdictions worldwide. We deliver our investment capabilities through a variety of products and vehicles and multiple points of access, including directly to investors and through financial intermediaries. Our investment products include our sponsored funds, as well as institutional and high-net-worth separate accounts, retail separately managed account programs, sub-advised products, and other investment vehicles. Our funds include registered funds (including exchange-traded funds, or "ETFs") and unregistered funds. Related services include applicable fund administration, sales and distribution, and shareholder servicing, which we may perform directly or outsource to third parties. We also provide sub-advisory services to certain investment products sponsored by other companies that may be sold to investors under the brand names of those other companies or on a co-branded basis.

We offer our clients the combined experience of our investment professionals with expertise across asset classes and a sharp focus on managing risk. We are committed to delivering strong investment performance for our clients, and to offering a broad range of strategies and drawing on our diverse experiences and perspectives gained through our long history in the investment management business. We know that success demands smart and effective business innovation, solutions and technologies, and we remain focused on investment excellence, innovating to meet evolving client goals, and building strong partnerships by delivering superior client service. We continue to focus on the long-term investment performance of our investment products and on providing high quality service to our clients.

The global business and regulatory environments in which we operate remain complex, uncertain and subject to change. We are subject to various laws, rules and regulations globally that impose restrictions, limitations, registration, reporting and disclosure requirements on our business, and add complexity to our global compliance operations. Incorporated herein by reference is certain financial information about our segment and geographic areas contained in Note 18 – Segment and Geographic Information in the notes to consolidated financial statements in Item 8 of Part II of this Annual Report.

Since 1947, the Company and its predecessors have been engaged in the investment management and related services business. Franklin was incorporated in the State of Delaware in November 1969, and originated our mutual fund business with the initial Franklin family of funds, known for its fixed income funds and growth and value-oriented equity funds. Over the years, we have expanded and developed our business to meet evolving investor needs, in part, by acquiring companies engaged in investment management and related services. We have added, among others: (i) the Templeton global investment firm in 1992, (ii) the Franklin Mutual Series investment firm in 1996, (iii) the Franklin Bissett Canadian investment firm in 2000, (iv) the Fiduciary Trust International investment and trust services firm in 2001, (v) the Benefit Street Partners alternative credit management firm in 2019, (vi) the Athena Capital Advisors investment and wealth management firm in March 2020, (vii) The Pennsylvania Trust Company investment and trust services firm in May 2020, (viii) the Legg Mason global investment firm in July 2020, (ix) the O'Shaughnessy Asset Management quantitative asset management firm in December 2021, (x) the Lexington Partners global alternatives investment firm in April 2022, (xi) the Alcentra alternative credit investment firm in November 2022, (xii) the Putnam global investment firm in January 2024, and (xiii) the Apera asset management firm in October 2025.

Through our subsidiaries, we are committed to helping investors navigate global markets, as well as continuing to evolve and build on our strengths to meet the needs of our clients. We generally derive our revenues and income from providing investment management and related services to our products and the products we sub-advise. Our investment management fees, which represent a majority of our revenues, depend to a large extent on the level and relative mix of our AUM and the types of services provided, which are subject to change.

Our business is conducted through our subsidiaries, including our specialist investment managers. Our specialist investment managers include subsidiaries registered with the United States ("U.S.") Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") as investment advisers under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"), as well as subsidiaries registered as investment adviser equivalents in jurisdictions including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Commonwealth of The Bahamas, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Japan, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Switzerland, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom ("U.K.") and Uzbekistan.

We offer a broad product mix under our equity, fixed income, alternative, multi-asset and cash management asset classes. Our equity capabilities include value, deep value, core value, blend, growth and growth at a reasonable price, convertibles, sector, Shariah, smart beta and thematic investments. Our fixed income capabilities include government, municipals, corporate credit, bank loans, securitized, multi-sector, and other investments. Our alternative capabilities include private debt, hedge funds, private equity, real estate and infrastructure investments. Our multi-asset capabilities include income, real return, balanced/hybrid, total return, target date/risk, absolute return, tactical asset allocation and managed volatility investments.

We believe, despite market risks, that we have a competitive advantage as a result of the economic and geographic diversity of our products available to our clients. Our U.S. funds include U.S. mutual funds, closed-end funds, ETFs, private funds, sub-advised funds and other products (including products we sub-advise and those sub-advised by third parties). Our non-U.S. funds include a variety of cross-border funds principally domiciled in Luxembourg or Ireland, registered for sale to non-U.S. investors in certain other countries, and international locally domiciled funds and products for the particular local market. Our institutional separate account services are provided to various institutions globally for which we serve as an investment adviser. Our retail separately managed accounts, commonly known as managed accounts or wrap programs, are sponsored by various financial institutions. We also offer and serve as investment adviser to various other products.

Our fees for providing investment management services are generally based on a percentage of AUM in the accounts that we advise, and vary based on the asset classes of the accounts, the types of services that we provide, and the market for those services.

headings: Volatility and disruption of our business and financial markets and adverse changes in the global economy may significantly affect our results of operations and put pressure on our financial results.
The amount and mix of our AUM are subject to significant fluctuations, and a shift in our asset mix toward lower-fee products may negatively impact our revenues and income.
Our funds may be subject to liquidity risks or an unanticipated large number of redemptions and fund closures.
Poor investment performance of our products could reduce the level of our AUM or affect our sales, and negatively impact our revenues and income.
Harm to our reputation may negatively impact our revenues and income.
Our business and operations are subject to adverse effects from the outbreak and spread of contagious diseases.
We may review and pursue strategic transactions that could pose risks to our business and global operations.
Our business operations are complex and a failure to perform operational tasks properly or comply with applicable regulatory requirements could have an adverse effect on our revenues and income.

Failure to establish adequate controls and risk management policies, or the circumvention of controls and policies, could have an adverse effect on our global operations, reputation and financial position.
We face risks, and corresponding potential costs and expenses, associated with conducting operations and growing our business in numerous countries.
Failure to properly address the increased transformative pressures affecting the investment management industry could negatively impact our business.
Increasing competition and other changes in the third-party distribution and sales channels on which we depend could reduce our revenues and income and hinder our growth.
Any failure of our third-party providers to fulfill their obligations, or our failure to maintain good relationships with our providers, could adversely impact our business.
We may be adversely affected if any of our third-party providers is subject to a successful cyber or security attack.
Our ability to manage and grow our business successfully can be impeded by systems and other technological limitations.

Our inability to recover successfully, should we experience a disaster or other business continuity problem, could cause material financial loss, regulatory actions, legal liability, and/or reputational harm.
Developing regulatory treatment of AI, and failure to adequately address AI-related challenges, creates a risk of reputational harm and an impediment to growth.
We depend on key personnel and our financial performance could be negatively affected by the loss of their services.
Our ability to meet cash needs depends upon certain factors, including the market value of our assets, our operating cash flows and our perceived creditworthiness.
We are dependent on the earnings of our subsidiaries.
We are subject to extensive, complex, overlapping and frequently changing rules, regulations, policies, and legal interpretations.
We may be adversely affected as a result of new or revised legislation or regulations or by changes in the interpretation of existing laws and regulations, in the U.S. and other jurisdictions.
Failure to comply with the laws, rules or regulations in any of the jurisdictions in which we operate could result in substantial harm to our reputation and results of operations.
Changes in tax laws or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could have a material impact on our financial condition, revenues and income.
Our contractual obligations may subject us to indemnification costs and liability to third parties.
Failure to protect our intellectual property may negatively impact our business.
paragraphs: We derive substantially all of our operating revenues and income from providing investment management and related services to investors in jurisdictions worldwide through our investment products, which include our funds, as well as institutional and high-net-worth separate accounts, retail separately managed account programs, sub-advised products, and other investment vehicles. Related services include fund administration, sales and distribution, and shareholder servicing, which we may perform directly or outsource to third parties. The investment management industry continues to experience disruption and challenges, including continued fee pressure, regulatory changes, an increasing and changing role of technology in investment management services, the continuous introduction of new products and services, and the consolidation of financial services firms through mergers and acquisitions. Further, financial markets have experienced and may continue, from time to time, to experience volatility and disruption worldwide. Declines in global economic markets have periodically resulted, and may continue to result, in significant decreases in our AUM, revenues and income, and future declines may further negatively impact our financial results. Such declines have had, and may in the future have, a material adverse impact on our business. We may need to modify our business, strategies or operations and we may be subject to additional constraints or costs in order to compete in a changing global economy and business environment.

Individual financial, equity, debt and commodity markets may be adversely affected by financial, economic, operational, political, electoral, diplomatic or other changes and/or instabilities that are particular to the country or region in which a market is located, including without limitation local acts of terrorism, economic crises, political protests, war, insurrection or other business, social or political crises. For example, the Ukraine-Russia and Middle East wars and/or conflicts may continue to develop and/or expand globally and significantly impact the global economy and financial markets, which may have an adverse effect on our investment performance and flows in certain products. Global economic conditions, exacerbated by war, terrorism, social, civil or political unrest, natural disasters, public health crises, such as epidemics or pandemics, or financial crises, changes in the equity, debt or commodity marketplaces or market operations, changes in currency exchange rates, interest rates, inflation rates, the yield curve, defaults by trading counterparties, bond defaults, revaluation and bond market liquidity risks, geopolitical risks, the imposition of economic sanctions and other factors that are difficult to predict, affect the mix, market values and levels of our AUM. Changing market conditions could also cause an impairment to the value of our goodwill and other intangible assets.

Fluctuations in the amount and mix of our AUM may be attributable in part to market conditions outside of our control that have had, and in the future could have, a negative impact on our revenues and income. The level of our revenues depends largely on the level and relative mix of AUM. Our investment management fee revenues are based primarily on a percentage of AUM and vary with the types and strategies of our products. Any decrease in the value or amount of our AUM because of market volatility or other factors, such as asset outflows or a decline in the price of securities, in particular market segments or in the securities market generally, negatively impacts our revenues and income. Changing market conditions and investor preferences may cause a shift in our asset mix toward certain lower fee products, such as fixed income products and ETFs, and away from higher fee equity and alternative products, which may cause a related decline in our revenues and income. In addition, increases in interest rates, particularly if rapid, as well as uncertainty in the future direction of interest rates, may have a negative impact on our fixed income products and decrease the total return on bond investments due to lower market valuations of existing bonds. Moreover, we generally derive higher investment management and distribution fees from our international products than from our U.S. products, and higher sales fees from our U.S. products than from our international products. Changing market conditions may cause a shift in our asset mix between international and U.S. products, which may result in a decline in our revenues and income.

Due to market volatility, reputational harm or other events or conditions described above, our funds may need to sell securities or instruments that they hold, possibly at a loss, or draw on any available lines of credit, to obtain cash to maintain sufficient liquidity or settle redemptions, or settle in-kind with securities held in the applicable fund. While we have no legal or contractual obligation to do so, we have in the past provided, and may in the future at our discretion

provide, financial support to our funds to enable them to maintain sufficient liquidity in any such event. Changes in investor preferences regarding our more popular products have in the past caused, and could in the future cause, sizable redemptions and lower the value of our AUM, which would result in lower revenue and operating results. Increased market volatility and changes in investor preferences also increase the risk of fund closures. Any decrease in the level of our AUM resulting from market declines, credit or interest rate volatility or uncertainty, increased redemptions or other factors could negatively impact our revenues and income.

paragraphs: Franklin Resources, Inc. ("Franklin") 為一間控股公司，其子公司以我們的 Franklin Templeton® 及/或子公司品牌名稱運作。Franklin 的普通股在紐約證券交易所 (the "NYSE") 交易，代碼為 "BEN"，並包含在 Standard & Poor's 500 指數中。在本年度報告中，Franklin 及其子公司 collectively 稱為 "Company"，並用 "we," "us," "our" 及其他相似詞語指代 Company。我們有一個運營分部，為投資管理及相關服務。

我們以我們各種不同的品牌名稱提供服務與產品，包括但不限於 Alcentra®, Apera®, Benefit Street Partners®, Brandywine Global Investment Management®, Canvas®, Clarion Partners®, ClearBridge Investments®, Fiduciary Trust International™, Franklin®, Franklin Mutual Series®, K2®, Legg Mason®, Lexington Partners®, O'Shaughnessy®, Putnam®, Royce®, Templeton® 及 Western Asset Management Company®。除非另有說明，我們的 "funds" 指的是我們各品牌名稱下所提供的基金，可能包含共用品牌基金。

我們是一家全球投資管理機構，截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日，管理資產規模 ("AUM") 超過 1.6 兆美元。我們的使命是透過投資管理專業、財富管理及科技解決方案，協助客戶實現更好的成果。透過我們的專業投資經理，我們在全球範圍內提供專業化服務，具備在股票、固定收益、另類投資及多資產解決方案方面的廣泛能力。在超過 75 年的時間裡，我們致力於為客戶提供卓越的投資管理服務，並發展出一項全球分散化的業務，包括透過戰略收購實現。

我們為全球各司法管轄區的零售、機構及高淨值投資者提供投資管理及相關服務。我們透過多種產品與工具及多個接觸點提供投資能力，包括直接對投資者及透過金融中介機構。我們的投資產品包括我們所贊助的基金，以及機構及高淨值分離帳戶、零售分離管理帳戶計畫、受託產品及其它投資工具。我們的基金包括註冊基金（包括交易所交易基金，或 "ETFs"）及未註冊基金。相關服務包括適用的基金行政、銷售與分佈及股東服務，我們可能直接執行或委外給第三方。我們也為其他公司所贊助的投資產品提供受託服務，這些產品可能以那些公司的品牌名稱銷售給投資者，或以共用品牌方式銷售。

我們為客戶提供投資專業人士的綜合經驗，他們在各類資產上具備專業知識，並專注於風險管理。我們致力於為客戶提供強勁的投資表現，並提供廣泛的策略，並透過我們在投資管理業務長達多年歷史中累積的多樣經驗與觀點。我們知道成功需要聰明且有效的商業創新、解決方案與科技，我們持續專注於投資卓越，創新以符合客戶目標的變化，並透過提供優秀的客戶服務建立強大的合作夥伴關係。我們持續專注於投資產品的長期投資表現，並為客戶提供高品質的服務。

我們所處的全球業務與監管環境仍然複雜、不確定且可能變化。我們受到全球各國法律、規則與規範的影響，這些規範對我們的業務施加限制、限制、註冊、報告與披露要求，並增加我們全球合規作業的複雜性。 herein by reference 納入了關於我們分部與地理區域的財務資訊，內容包含在 Note 18 – Segment and Geographic Information 的附註中，位於本年度報告 Item 8 of Part II 的合併財務陳述書附註中。

自 1947 年以來，本公司及其前身一直從事投資管理與相關服務業務。Franklin 於 1969 年 11 月在特拉華州註冊成立，並以最初的 Franklin 家族基金開始我們的共同基金業務，這些基金以固定收益基金及成長與價值導向的股票基金聞名。多年來，我們擴展並發展業務以符合投資者需求，部分透過收購從事投資管理與相關服務的公司。我們已收購的公司包括：(i) 1992 年收購的 Templeton 全球投資公司，(ii) 1996 年收購的 Franklin Mutual Series 投資公司，(iii) 2000 年收購的 Franklin Bissett 加拿大投資公司，(iv) 2001 年收購的 Fiduciary Trust International 投資與信託服務公司，(v) 2019 年收購的 Benefit Street Partners 另類信貸管理公司，(vi) 2020 年 3 月收購的 Athena Capital Advisors 投資與財富管理公司，(vii) 2020 年 5 月收購的 The Pennsylvania Trust Company 投資與信託服務公司，(viii) 2020 年 7 月收購的 Legg Mason 全球投資公司，(ix) 2021 年 12 月收購的 O'Shaughnessy Asset Management 量化資產管理公司，(x) 2022 年 4 月收購的 Lexington Partners 全球另類投資公司，(xi) 2022 年 11 月收購的 Alcentra 另類信貸投資公司，(xii) 2024 年 1 月收購的 Putnam 全球投資公司，以及 (xiii) 2025 年 10 月收購的 Apera 資產管理公司。
透過我們的子公司，我們致力於協助投資者應對全球市場，並持續進化與建立我們的優勢以符合客戶需求。我們通常透過為我們的產品及我們受託的產品提供投資管理與相關服務來獲取收入與利潤。我們的投資管理費用，代表我們收入的大多數，很大程度上取決於我們 AUM 的水準與相對組成，以及所提供的服務類型，這些都可能有所變化。

本公司業務透過子公司進行，包括專門投資經理。本公司專門投資經理包括已向美國（"U.S.")證券交易委員會（"SEC"）登記為根據1940年投資顧問法（"Advisers Act"）投資顧問的子公司，以及在澳洲、巴西、加拿大、中國、巴哈馬聯邦、香港、愛爾蘭、印度、日本、盧森堡、馬來西亞、墨西哥、沙烏地阿拉伯、新加坡、瑞士、韓國、阿拉伯聯合大公國、英國（"U.K."）及烏茲別克斯坦等司法管轄區登記為投資顧問等同的子公司。

我們在股權、固定收益、另類投資、多資產及現金管理資產類別下提供廣泛的產品組合。我們的股權能力包括價值、深度價值、核心價值、混合、成長及合理價格成長、轉換債券、產業、 Shariah、智慧β及主題投資。我們的固定收益能力包括政府債券、市政債券、企業信用、銀行貸款、證券化、多產業及其它投資。我們的另類投資能力包括私人債務、避險基金、私人股權、不動產及基礎設施投資。我們的多資產能力包括收入、實質回報、平衡/混合、總回報、目標日期/風險、絕對回報、資產配置及管理波動性投資。

我們認為，儘管市場風險，我們因可提供給客戶的產品具有經濟及地理多樣性，而擁有競爭優勢。我們的美國基金包括美國共同基金、封閉式基金、ETF、私人基金、子經理基金及其他產品（包括我們子經理及第三方子經理的產品）。我們的非美國基金包括多種跨境基金，主要設立於盧森堡或愛爾蘭，並在某些國家註冊銷售給非美國投資者，以及針對特定當地市場的國際本地設立基金及產品。我們的機構獨立帳戶服務提供給全球各機構，我們擔任投資顧問。我們的零售獨立管理帳戶，常見為管理帳戶或包裝方案，由各金融機構發起。我們也提供並擔任投資顧問於各種其他產品。
我們提供投資管理服務的費用通常根據我們管理帳戶的總資產規模（AUM）百分比計算，並根據帳戶的資產類別、我們提供的服務類型及市場情況而有所不同。

headings: 本公司業務與財務市場的波動性與幹擾，以及全球經濟的不利變化，可能顯著影響我們的營運結果，並對財務結果造成壓力。
本公司管理的資產規模（AUM）數量與組成可能出現顯著波動，若資產組成向低費用產品轉移，可能對我們的營業收入與獲利產生負面影響。
本公司基金可能面臨流動性風險，或遭遇預期之外的大規模贖回與基金關閉。
本公司產品的投資表現不佳，可能降低本公司管理的資產規模（AUM），或影響銷售，並對營業收入與獲利產生負面影響。
本公司聲譽受損，可能對營業收入與獲利產生負面影響。
本公司業務與營運可能因傳染性疾病爆發與擴散而受到不利影響。
本公司可能審視並進行戰略交易，這些交易可能對本公司業務與全球營運造成風險。
本公司業務營運複雜，若未能妥善執行營運任務或符合適用的監管要求，可能對營業收入與獲利產生不利影響。
未能建立適當的控制制度及風險管理政策，或規避這些控制制度及政策，可能對我們的全球營運、聲譽及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們在多個國家進行營運並擴展業務，面臨相關風險，以及對應的潛在成本與費用。
未能妥善應對影響投資管理業的增加性轉型壓力，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
第三方分銷與銷售通路的競爭增加及其他變動，可能降低我們的營收與獲利，並阻礙我們的成長。
若我們的第三方服務供應商未能履行其義務，或我們未能維持與供應商的良好關係，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
若任何第三方服務供應商遭受成功的網路或安全攻擊，我們可能因此受到不利影響。
我們管理及成長業務的能力，可能因系統及其他科技限制而受阻。
若我們遭遇災難或其他業務持續性問題，而無法成功復原，可能導致重大財務損失、監管行動、法律責任及/或聲譽損害。
發展中對人工智能（AI）的規範處理，以及未能充分應對與AI相關的挑戰，會造成聲譽損害並阻礙成長。
我們依賴關鍵人員，其服務的流失可能對我們的財務表現產生負面影響。
我們滿足現金需求的能力取決於若干因素，包括我們資產的市場價值、營運現金流以及我們的信用評等。
我們依賴子公司的營收。
我們受到廣泛、複雜、重疊且頻繁變更的規則、法規、政策及法律解釋的影響。
由於美國及其他司法管轄區的新法或修法，或現有法律與法規解釋的變更，我們可能受到負面影響。
未能遵守我們營運所在任何司法管轄區的法律、規則或法規，可能對我們的聲譽及營運成果造成重大損害。
稅法的變更或面臨額外所得稅負擔，可能對我們的財務狀況、營收及所得產生重大影響。
我方之契約義務可能使我們需承擔賠償費用及對第三方之責任。
未能保護我方之智慧財產權可能對我方業務產生負面影響。
paragraphs: 我們幾乎所有的營運收入及獲利皆來自於為全球各地的投資人提供投資管理及相關服務，透過我們的投資產品，包括基金、機構及高淨值個別帳戶、零售個別管理帳戶計畫、受託產品及其它投資工具。相關服務包括基金後臺管理、銷售與分銷，以及股東服務，我們可能直接執行或委外給第三方。投資管理產業持續面臨顛覆與挑戰，包括持續的費用壓力、法規變動、科技在投資管理服務中日益增加且變化的角色、新產品與服務的持續推出，以及透過合併與收購金融服務機構的整併。此外，金融市場已歷經並可能持續在某些時間點經歷波動與顛覆。全球經濟市場的下滑已 periodically 結果，且可能持續導致我們的 AUM、收入及獲利顯著下降，未來的下滑可能進一步對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。此等下滑已對我們的業務產生，且可能在未來對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。我們可能需要修改我們的業務、策略或運作，我們也可能面臨額外的限制或成本，以在變動的全球經濟與商業環境中競爭。

個別金融、股權、債務及商品市場可能因特定國家或地區市場所在地的金融、經濟、運作、政治、選舉、外交或其他變動及/或不穩定而受到不利影響，包括但不限於當地的恐怖攻擊、經濟危機、政治抗議、戰爭、起義或其他商業、社會或政治危機。例如，烏克蘭與俄羅斯及中東戰爭及/或衝突可能持續發展及/或擴展至全球，並對全球經濟與金融市場產生重大影響，這可能對我們某些產品的投資績效與資金流產生不利影響。全球經濟狀況因戰爭、恐怖主義、社會、內亂或政治不穩定、自然災害、公共衛生危機（如疫情或大流行），或金融危機、股權、債務或商品市場或市場運作的變動、貨幣兌換率、利率、通貨膨脹率、收益率曲線、交易對手違約、債券違約、重新評價及債券市場流動性風險、地緣政治風險、經濟制裁的施加及其他難以預測的因素而影響我們 AUM 的組成、市場價值及水準。

我們 AUM 的數量與組成的變動可能部分歸因於我們無法控制的市場條件，這些條件已對我們的收入及獲利產生負面影響，未來也可能產生負面影響。我們收入的水準 largely 取決於 AUM 的水準與相對組成。我們的投資管理費用收入主要基於 AUM 的百分比，並隨著我們產品的類型與策略而變動。任何因市場波動或其他因素（如資產流出或特定市場區段或整體證券市場的證券價格下跌）導致我們 AUM 的價值或數量下降，會對我們的收入及獲利產生負面影響。變動的市場條件與投資人偏好可能導致我們的資產組成向某些費用較低的產品（如固定收益產品與 ETFs）轉移，並遠離費用較高的股權與另類產品，這可能導致我們的收入及獲利相應下降。此外，利率的上升，特別是如果快速上升，以及未來利率方向的不確定性，可能對我們的固定收益產品產生負面影響，並因現有債券的市場價值降低而減少債券投資的總回報。此外，我們通常從國際產品中獲得較高的投資管理與分銷費用，而從美國產品中獲得較高的銷售費用。變動的市場條件可能導致我們國際與美國產品之間的資產組成轉移，這可能導致我們的收入及獲利下降。
由於市場波動、聲譽損害或其他上述所述事件或條件，我們的基金可能需要出售其所持有的證券或工具，可能以虧損為代價，或動用任何可用的信用線，以取得現金以維持足夠的流動性或兌現紅利，或以所持有的證券進行現金兌換。雖然我們沒有法律或契約義務必須這樣做，但我們過去曾提供，且可能在未來根據我們的判斷提供財務支援給我們的基金，以使其在任何這種情況下維持足夠的流動性。
投資人對我們較受歡迎產品的偏好變動已過去曾導致，且可能在未來導致大量贖回，並降低我們的 AUM 值，這將導致收入與營運結果下降。增加的市場波動與投資人偏好變動也會增加基金關閉的風險。任何因市場下跌、信貸或利率波動或不確定性、增加的贖回或其他因素導致我們 AUM 水準下降的情況，都可能對我們的收入與獲利產生負面影響。
